For an accepted nonzero fractional shift, bilinear warpAffine changes RGB sample values; channel reversal preserves those differences, and sufficiently large interpolation changes survive clipping, multiplication by 255, rounding, and uint8 conversion. Thus the intervention is observably nontrivial after the exact mandatory conversion, although guarded or zero estimates can leave individual inputs unchanged. Its causal mechanism is LR-guided estimation and correction of one continuous global spatial translation. That is mechanistically distinct from every stopped route: it neither combines predictions nor performs photometric residual correction, frequency shrinkage, contrast/gamut adjustment, phase-locked additive correction, lattice selection, or clipping-only projection. Shared use of BT.601 luminance, LR guidance, interpolation, or image-global estimation does not make those different transformations the same mechanism.

routes.reason: Estimates and applies a spatial translation to one prediction; it does not flip, average, or otherwise ensemble predictions.
Uses LR only to estimate geometry; it does not compute, upsample, or add an LR photometric residual.
Spatial resampling after translation is not gated attenuation of weak high-frequency coefficients.
A coordinate translation does not expand luminance deviations around a global center.
It does not compress chroma toward luminance or project colors into gamut along a constant-luminance axis.
It estimates continuous global displacement rather than subtracting additive offsets indexed by a 2x2 phase pattern.
It does not select among enclosing RGB quantization-lattice corners.
The warp can alter in-range samples before conversion and is not merely clipping already performed by the evaluator.
Global geometric registration is distinct from BT.601-luminance-preserving out-of-gamut chroma compression.
Global geometric registration is distinct from luminance-preserving nearest RGB lattice selection.
It performs no per-pixel search among eight RGB lattice corners or RGB-distance tie-breaking.
Its intervention is a spatial warp, not fixed componentwise projection onto [0,1].
It corrects a continuous image-global coordinate displacement, not a robustly estimated zero-sum additive 2x2 luminance bias.
